speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat1 had also asked a related question for the Sitting on or after 21 October 2022.

speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Desmond Lee)
text: So, with your permission, Sir, may I take these three questions together?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The HDB resale price index, or RPI, had declined by 9.9% over five years, between 2014 and 2018, and remained flat in 2019.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The increase in resale HDB flat prices during the last two years of the pandemic reflects broad-based demand for housing, supported by the previously low interest rate environment.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In December 2021, the Government announced a package of measures to cool the private residential and HDB resale markets, including tightening the loan-to-value, or LTV limit, for loans from HDB.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In the immediate quarters, following the implementation of these measures, the HDB resale price index reflected a lower increase of 2.4% in 1Q2022, and 2.8% in 2Q2022, compared to 3.4% in 4Q2021.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Government has been watching the property market closely.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Sustained property price increases, if left unchecked, could run ahead of our economic fundamentals and increase the risk of a destabilising correction later, which will adversely impact many existing home owners.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We expect these measures to slow the pace of HDB resale price increases, but we will continue to monitor the housing market closely.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: One of the measures that we have implemented is the 15-month wait-out period before current and former private residential property owners can buy a non-subsidised HDB resale flat, that means, without taking the CPF housing grant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Alex Yam asked how this measure will help to cool the HDB resale market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: We will review this measure after monitoring overall demand and market conditions.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: To be clear, the 15-month wait-out period is a new measure for those buying resale flats without grant.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: There is an existing long-standing measure for private property owners buying HDB resale flats with grant, and they have to wait out 30 months.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This measure, the long-standing measure, has been in place since 1975.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Members have asked about the number of private property owners who may be affected by this new wait-out period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This group, which includes those who had sold their private property up to 15 months before their resale flat application, accounts for about one in 10 resale flat buyers in the past three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Proportionately, more current and former private property owners pay COV, or Cash-Over-Valuation, compared to other resale flat buyers, and they also pay higher COV amounts.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This is, generally, because many of these private property owners have more financial means to pay for their resale flats, compared to first-time flat buyers or HDB upgraders.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some may not even need to take housing loans to complete their flat purchase.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Alex Yam asked about the assistance provided to home seekers who own or have recently disposed of, their private property, but who urgently need housing support.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Indeed, we recognise that not all private property owners are in exactly the same situation and not all have the same financial means.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And that is why, to support this group, we had introduced two measures when we made this move to introduce the new wait-out period.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: First, we exempted seniors who are moving from private property to a 4-room or smaller resale flat from the wait-out period, if both the senior and his spouse are 55 years old and above.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: This helps our seniors right-size their homes and improve their retirement adequacy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: These seniors make up about three in 10 of the private property owners who had bought resale HDB flats in the past three years.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Of these seniors, slightly less than one in five also paid a COV when buying a resale flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, that is the first – the exemption for seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Second, regardless of their age, current and former private property owners who face extenuating circumstances can approach HDB for assistance and we will assess their situation on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Pursuant to this, HDB received some 650 appeals since the wait-out period was introduced.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Two hundred and twenty of these home seekers had obtained an Option to Purchase (OTP) to buy an HDB resale flat before the wait-out period was put in place.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For these home seekers, HDB has exercised flexibility and waived the 15-month wait-out period for all of them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: A second group of home seekers are those who have not obtained an OTP to buy an HDB resale flat, but who may have committed to sell or have recently sold their existing private property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB will assess these appeals on a case-by-case basis.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Mr Saktiandi Supaat asked about the possible impact of this move on the HDB resale market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I explained earlier, the aim of this move is to moderate demand from private property owners cashing out and going to the HDB resale market, in order to give priority to first time home buyers, particularly during this period.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: I have one supplementary question for the Minister.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: With regard to one of the two exceptions, for those who are 55 years old and above, there is an exception made for them to purchase 4-room flats and lower, I would like to ask the Minister if MND believes that this may inadvertently also drive up prices in the smaller flat-size market – because, I think, the figure that was quoted earlier was three in 10 are in this category.

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Therefore, do MND and HDB see that there might be a rise in demand for the smaller flat types?

speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: Ultimately, I think the cooling measures are important and I think it bears reiterating that MND remains committed to providing Singaporeans with affordable and attainable homes over the longer term.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The private property market has gone up, an increasing number appear to have sold their private properties and to move into HDB flats.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: For seniors, we recognise that many of them want to do this in order to enhance their retirement adequacy – they want to right-size, they want to manage their financial situation as they go into retirement.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, we made this carve-out for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And as for why it is a 4-room flat and smaller, if your aim is to prepare for retirement and to enhance your retirement adequacy, then going to a smaller flat will give our seniors even more financial space, as they right-size from a private property to a smaller flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I have said earlier, the private property owners or former private property owners moving into the HDB resale market make up about one in 10 of resale flat buyers over the last three years and, out of that group, seniors make up a smaller portion of that.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, three in 10 of that one in 10 are seniors above the age of 55 and, so, they are a smaller subset of the private property owners moving into the HDB resale market.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Therefore, we will continue to watch and monitor the property market carefully and monitor the effects of the moves that we have made.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: One is, the Minister mentioned that there will be an enhancement, potentially, in terms of land sales for supply of flats, going forward.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: This would be in relation to my question about how the reduction of supply of private property in the market could drive HDB upgraders to splurge on resale flats.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: So, my first question is, to what extent will that land sale lead to further increases in resale flats and what type of resale flats could that possibly be?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: My second supplementary question is, with the higher interest rate environment, will there be significant impact in the context of this current environment to impact certain demographics, for example, like what the previous Member had mentioned about seniors, but also young individuals or young families?

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: Will the high interest rates lead to further impact on them, going forward, into buying these resale flats?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member was concerned whether this wait-out period, which aims to moderate demand for resale flats by putting a wait-out period for private property owners coming into the resale market through the wait-out period; his concern is whether that would potentially reduce the supply of private properties on the private resale market and, hence, cause HDB upgraders who are actually wanting to buy those units, to then buy a bigger HDB resale flat and then exacerbating the condition.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: HDB upgraders, firstly, I think, some of them will have an intention to upgrade from HDB to private property.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: You cannot rule out that some HDB upgraders will, of course, want to upgrade to a larger HDB flat.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, every HDB upgrader will have their own objectives and their own aspirations.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But be that as it may, HDB upgraders will continue to have a wide range of options, which include HDB flats of varying sizes and across various locations, as well as new and existing private properties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: The Member also asked whether the higher interest rate environment will have a differential impact on different groups.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, of course, we adjusted the loan-to-value, in order to protect home buyers who need to leverage and take loans in order to buy.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But there is also an impact on existing home owners who were servicing their loans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Some of them are on fixed interest rates and the banks have mostly stopped these fixed interest rate plans for residential properties.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Then, the groups that are on adjustable interest rate loans, some come with a time lag, some follow the market and market interest rates immediately and some take HDB loans.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, obviously, for these different groups, they will feel the impact either at different times or immediately.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: And, therefore, this will impact the groups differently.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: In terms of their outlay, they will have to stump up more in order to service their monthly mortgages.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Would the Government consider exempting Singaporeans with genuine financial difficulties from the effect of the property cooling measures?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: The reason I am saying this is because these people may have difficulty servicing their existing loans for their condos, they may have existing debt issues arising from their own other financial obligations and they have no choice but to dispose of their current private property and they need a place to stay, they need a place to live.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, they need to buy an HDB property and they may not be able to afford commercial rental.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: As I said, there are two exemption measures.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: They can approach HDB and we will see how to help them.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, if the Member has come across any of them, please let us know.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: There is a wait-out period of 15 months; so, will there be an impact on the rental market because these residents probably will have to find HDB flats for rental?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: As a result, this might drive up the rental prices.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Certainly, those who own an existing private property and intend to wait out that period would find alternative accommodation, either to reside with family or rent.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: So, there will be those choices that will have to be made because of the implementation of this new measure.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: At the same time, it may also cause private property owners who are not seniors waiting to retire or, as Member Dennis Tan had mentioned, people who have financial situation.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: If they are thinking about whether to make this move now, this might cause them to postpone their decision.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: It achieves the effect also of moderating demand for resale flats at this time and gives priority to first-time home buyers who may be looking to the resale market for their first home.
